messages.subject: R 3.5 StatET Data Viewer - data.table cedta stack trace in console - With Fix!
messages.subject_clean: R 3.5 StatET Data Viewer - data.table cedta stack trace in console - With Fix!
messages.body_plain:
With the new rj update, R 3.5 is working well for me with StatET on Windows!

There was one minor issue with data.table (not really with StatET or rj 
as such).

Every time I viewed a data.table in the data viewer (or paged up and 
down within a data.table), I was getting a long error trace in the 
console (see bottom of this post).

Fortunately, I was able to fix the problem by executing the following line:
assignInNamespace("cedta.override", c(data.table:::cedta.override,"rj"), 
"data.table")

(which I derived from this post:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/13106018/data-table-error-when-used-through-knitr-gwidgetswww 
)

A request could be made to the data.table developers to add rj to the 
default built in list of overrides so that this is not necessary.  
(Actually we always got a one line error in prior versions but now with 
this trace it became more urgent to fix).


======================================
Error output in Console prior to applying fix:

cedta decided 'rj' wasn't data.table aware. Call stack with [[1L]] applied:
[[1]]
function (expr, ..., finally)
{
     tryCatchList <- function(expr, names, parentenv, handlers) {
         nh <- length(names)
         if (nh > 1L)
             tryCatchOne(tryCatchList(expr, names[-nh], parentenv,
                 handlers[-nh]), names[nh], parentenv, handlers[[nh]])
         else if (nh == 1L)
             tryCatchOne(expr, names, parentenv, handlers[[1L]])
         else expr
     }
     tryCatchOne <- function(expr, name, parentenv, handler) {
         doTryCatch <- function(expr, name, parentenv, handler) {
             .Internal(.addCondHands(name, list(handler), parentenv,
                 environment(), FALSE))
             expr
         }
         value <- doTryCatch(return(expr), name, parentenv, handler)
         if (is.null(value[[1L]])) {
             msg <- .Internal(geterrmessage())
             call <- value[[2L]]
             cond <- simpleError(msg, call)
         }
         else if (is.character(value[[1L]])) {
             msg <- value[[1L]]
             call <- value[[2L]]
             cond <- simpleError(msg, call)
         }
         else cond <- value[[1L]]
         value[[3L]](cond)
     }
     if (!missing(finally))
         on.exit(finally)
     handlers <- list(...)
     classes <- names(handlers)
     parentenv <- parent.frame()
     if (length(classes) != length(handlers))
         stop("bad handler specification")
     tryCatchList(expr, classes, parentenv, handlers)
}

messages.subject: Re: R 3.5 StatET Data Viewer - data.table cedta stack trace in console - With Fix!
messages.subject_clean: R 3.5 StatET Data Viewer - data.table cedta stack trace in console - With Fix!
messages.body_plain:
More good news:    With this fix
assignInNamespace("cedta.override", c(data.table:::cedta.override,"rj"), 
"data.table")
column widths in data.tables in the Data Viewer now are fitted 
correctly!  This is a tremendous improvement!

The reason must be that StatET must already have code to fit the column 
widths to the contents, but was being spoiled when data.table dumbed 
down the data to lowest common denominator format because it thought it 
was being called by a dumb caller.

cedta stands for "Calling Environment is Data Table Aware."  It was 
defaulting to assuming StatET's Data Viewer was not Data Table aware.  
Evidently it is data.table aware.  Can we notify the data.table 
maintainers of that?   .  Alternatively there is a way it can detect 
that automatically - see 
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/10527072/using-data-table-package-inside-my-own-package 
.

Thanks.

messages.subject: controlling the packages lib locations to index by StatET
messages.subject_clean: controlling the packages lib locations to index by StatET
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm struggling with statET to index custom library folders.
By experimenting with the settings I came to a point where only the core
packages are now indexed, even if I reindex everything, though:

> .libPaths()
[1] "/usr/local/lib/R/site-library" "/usr/local/lib/R/library"
> .Library
[1] "/usr/local/lib/R/library"
> .Library.site
[1] "/usr/local/lib/R/site-library"

I tried to look at the statET source code, I saw that there were
differences when the R session is remote or not.

So my question is: in the case of a local R session (R console), which
settings of the R configuration determine the folders that will be
considered for indexing ?

I also kind of remember noticing a difference when paths were symbolic
links (that I now try to avoid). Is it possible ?

Thanks,
Karl

P.S
eclipse 4.4.2
Java Rj:  2.0.4.b201511061600E44sw
StatET for R    3.5.1.b201511061600E44sw
rj R package:  2.0.5-2
on Debian GNU/Linux 8.10 (jessie)
